texts.preamble: Ramnarain vs State Of M.P. on 16 November, 2017 1 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.] High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat Jabalpur Single Bench: Hon. Shri Justice G.S. Ahluwalia Criminal Revision No.792/1999 .........Applicant: Ramnarain Versus .........Respondent: State of M.P. Shri Ajay Tamrakar, Counsel for the applicant. Shri Manish Awasthy, Public Prosecutor for respondent/State. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Date of hearing : 16/11/2017 Date of order : 16/11/2017
texts.facts: He after going through the record, argued the matter on behalf of the applicant. The necessary facts for the disposal of the present revision in short are that on 27-2-1988 at about 9:30 A.M., the Food Inspector, S.C.Gupta found that the applicant was going in front of Usha Restaurant, Begumganj and was carrying 4 liters of milk for selling purposes. A notice for purchasing milk was given in Form No. 6, Ex. P.7, and after making payment of Rs.3/-, he Ramnarain vs State Of M.P. on 16 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81425364/ 1 purchased 750 M.L. of milk from the applicant. Thereafter, the purchased milk was made homogeneous. The milk was stored in clean and dry glass bottles and after adding 20 drops of Formalin, labels Ex.P.8 were affixed. The signatures of the applicant and two independent witnesses were obtained on the label. The Panchnama of the proceedings Ex. P.9 was prepared. One bottle along with form No.7 was sent to Public Analyst, Bhopal on 29-2-1988. The remaining two bottles were deposited in the office of Local Health Authority, Raisen. The milk was found adulterated. Permission was obtained for prosecution. Notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Ex. P.17, was sent by registered post, and the postal receipt is Ex. P.18. The complaint was filed against the applicant on 23-5-1988. The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty. The prosecution in order to prove its case, examined S.C. Gupta (P.W.1), Bhagirath Prasad (P.W.2). The applicant examined P.P. Gupta (D.W.1) in his defence. S.C. Gupta (P.W.1) has stated that he was appointed as Sanitary Inspector and the State Govt. by notification, Ex. P.1, had appointed all the Sanitary Inspectors as Food Inspector. The Dy. Directors have been given authority to grant sanction by notification Ex. P.5. He was going towards Begumganj town. On query, the applicant informed that he was carrying cow-buffalow mixed milk and is selling the same at the rate of Rs.4/- per liter. The applicant agreed to sell 750 M.L. of milk for a consideration of Rs.3/-. The consideration amount was paid and receipt Ex. P.6 was obtained. The milk was made homogeneous and milk was stored in three dry and clean bottles and 20 drops of formalin were added in each bottle. Labels were affixed and the signatures of the applicant and the independent witnesses were obtained and the panchnama Ex.P.9 was prepared. It is further stated that one sample was sent to the Public Analyst along with Form No.7 Ex.P.10. The seal was also sent. The acknowledgment of receipt of sample by the office of Public Analyst is Ex.P.12 and the Local Authority letter is Ex.P.13. The report of the Public Analyst is Ex.P.14, according to which, the milk was found adulterated. The permission for 4 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.] prosecution was sought by letter Ex. P.15 and the permission is Ex. P.16.
